test_cases.title: A requester cannot approve their own request from either the request page or a direct approval URL
test_cases.preconditions: A fictional pending request belongs to the current requester. The approval URL is supplied by a fixture, never guessed.

steps.action: Sign in as the requester test role and open the owned pending request.
steps.expected: The request details are visible and the Approve control is absent.

steps.action: Open the fixture-provided approval URL for the same request.
steps.expected: Access is denied; the request remains pending.

steps.action: Read the request state through the approved test fixture.
steps.expected: No approval decision or approver has been recorded.

steps.action: Open the audit entry for the denied attempt as an authorized auditor.
steps.expected: The attempt is recorded as denied without any approval event.

test_cases.title: A delayed confirmation does not present a timed-out submission as either failed or successfully completed
test_cases.preconditions: The stub accepts a request but delays the response beyond the client timeout.

steps.action: Submit a valid fictional request with the controlled timeout fixture.
steps.expected: A confirmation-pending message appears after the timeout.

steps.action: Inspect the request status panel before the delayed response is resolved.
steps.expected: The interface does not label the request failed or complete.

steps.action: Resolve the fixture's status lookup to the accepted request.
steps.expected: The original request identifier is displayed once, with no duplicate submission.

test_cases.title: Approval evidence identifies the exact request revision that the reviewer approved
test_cases.preconditions: The request belongs to another user and has frozen revision r7.

steps.action: Open request revision r7 as an eligible reviewer.
steps.expected: The review summary identifies revision r7.

steps.action: Approve the request with the standard decision action.
steps.expected: The decision is saved and its status becomes approved.
Actor, timestamp with offset, request ID and revision r7 are present.

test_cases.title: Repeated submission with an existing idempotency key returns the original request identifier
test_cases.preconditions: A deterministic request fixture provides an idempotency key and an accepted original request.

steps.action: Submit the request using the fixture's idempotency key.
Repeat the same payload and key.
steps.expected: The original identifier is returned, not a second request.

steps.action: Inspect the confirmation panel and request count.
steps.expected: The original identifier is displayed and exactly one request exists.

test_cases.title: Rejecting a request requires an explanation and preserves the draft when validation fails
test_cases.preconditions: A reviewer test identity must authenticate successfully; this prerequisite was unavailable in the sample run.

steps.action: Open the rejection form for an eligible pending request.
steps.expected: The explanation field is labelled and initially empty.

steps.action: Attempt rejection with a blank explanation.
steps.expected: Validation identifies the field; no decision is saved.

steps.action: Enter a reason and submit the rejection.
steps.expected: The rejection and exact explanation are recorded once.

test_cases.title: An authorized reviewer downloads the selected attachment using its original filename
test_cases.preconditions: The request has a synthetic attachment named supporting-note.txt and the reviewer has access.

steps.action: Open the evidence list for the request.
steps.expected: The synthetic attachment name and type are visible.
A file is delivered with the filename supporting-note.txt.

steps.action: Compare the delivered file with the synthetic fixture.
steps.expected: The content matches the fixture and no additional attachment is delivered.

sources.title: Harbor service request rules
sources.origin: Synthetic requirements authored for this design sample
sources.excerpt: 4.1 Requesters must not approve their own requests, including via direct routes. Denied attempts create an audit event. 4.3 Every approval stores the actor, timestamp and exact request revision. 4.4 Auditors can inspect but cannot edit or approve. 4.7 Rejection requires a non-empty explanation and must retain the form on validation failure. 4.8 Authorized attachment downloads preserve the original filename and content.

sources.title: Submission and confirmation contract
sources.origin: Synthetic API contract authored for this design sample
sources.excerpt: 2.3 A timeout after server acceptance leaves confirmation pending until a status lookup resolves it; the UI must not claim success or failure prematurely. 2.4 Repeating a payload with its accepted idempotency key returns the original request identifier and creates no duplicate.

sources.title: Working-day scheduling policy
sources.origin: Synthetic operations policy authored for this design sample
sources.excerpt: 3.2 Requests scheduled on a non-working day move to the next working day in the configured, versioned calendar. The chosen date is shown before confirmation.
